One of the four Indian Buddhist tenet systems, which asserts that forms of physical phenomena do not exist externally, coming from different natal sources than those of the minds that cognize them. Externally existing physical phenomena do not act as a natal source of the mental appearances (mental holograms) of them that arise in the cognition of them. The source of these mental appearances is only the mind -- or, more specifically, only the karmic tendency (karmic seed) for cognition of them, which is imputed on a mental continuum. The karmic tendency is the "natal source" of all aspects of the cognition of forms of physical phenomena: both the mental appearance as well as the consciousness and accompanying mental factors. Moreover, the mind (namely, the mental continuum on which the karmic tendency for cognition of these forms is imputable) has truly established existence.

fields.Definition: The first one out of the nine stages of settling the mind into a state of shamatha. Setting the mind on the object of focus. At this stage, we are merely able to set or place our attention on the object of focus, but are unable to maintain it.

The second one out of the nine stages of settling the mind into a state of shamatha. Here, we are able to maintain our mental hold on the object with some continuity, but only for a short time before losing it. It takes some time before we recognize that we have lost the object and before we can reestablish our focus.

The third one out of the nine stages of settling the mind into a state of shamatha. Here, we are able to recognize as soon as we have lost our mental hold on the object, and we are able to reset or restore our focus immediately.

The fourth one out of the nine stages of settling the mind into a state of shamatha. Here, we do not lose our mental hold on the object, but because the subtle mental flightiness of an undercurrent of thought and middling dullness are strong dangers and can still occur, we need to maintain their opponents very strongly.

The fifth one out of the nine stages of settling the mind into a state of shamatha. Here, we no longer experience gross flightiness, the subtle flightiness of an undercurrent of thought, or gross or middling dullness. However, because we have overstrained to concentrate and have sunk too deeply inwards, we have relaxed the appearance-producing factor giving rise to the appearance of the object of focus. Consequently, we experience subtle dullness. We need to refresh and uplift the mental hold by remembering the benefits of gaining shamatha.

The sixth one out of the nine stages of settling the mind into a state of shamatha. Here, although there is no longer great danger of subtle mental dullness, nevertheless in uplifting the mind, we became too excited and the mental hold became too tight. Consequently, we experience the subtle flightiness of itchiness to leave the object of focus. We need to use strong alertness to detect this and to relax our mental hold slightly.

The seventh one out of the nine stages of settling the mind into a state of shamatha. Here, although the danger of subtle flightiness or dullness is minimal, we still need to exert effort to rid ourselves of them completely.

The last one out of the nine stages of settling the mind into a state of shamatha. Here, we are able effortlessly to maintain concentration, free of any interruptions, throughout the entire session. This is the attainment of absorbed concentration.

fields.Definition: Ten factors that describe a precious human rebirth or situations in which such a rebirth occur and which enable an optimal level of Dharma practice. They include five personal situations and five social situations. The five personal enriching situations are rebirth as a human, in a central Buddhist region, with complete physical and mental faculties, still not experiencing the repercussions from having committed the most extreme destructive actions, and with instinctive belief in what is true. The five social enriching situations are rebirth where and when a Buddha has come, a Buddha has taught the Dharma, the Dharma is still maintained, with a monastic community following the Buddha’s example and with others compassionately supporting the monastic community.

Question: What does the word "Matters" here mean? In the dictionary there are many different variants. Unfortunately, i don't know where is this word from. Probably we shouldn't deal with it now, but we have this word in our old dictionary, that was composed long ago.

fields.Explanation:
Question: Our current variant is "Middle-Length Instructions". Since the word "discourse" has many meanings, please explain is our tanslation is OK or not.
ALEX: THIS IS THE PALI "MAJJHIMA-NIKAYA" NIKAYA MEANS A COLLECTION, AND HERE IT IS LITERALLY "A COLLECTION OF MIDDLE-LENGTH (SUTTAS)." THE MOST WELL-KNOWN ENGLISH TRANSLATION IS CALLED 'MIDDLE-LENGTH DISCOURSES" DISCOURSE MEANS A TEACHING, AND SO THAT IS OK SINCE THESE ARE TEXTS. THERE ARE ALSO THE DIGHA-NIKAYA (USUALLY TRANSLATED AS LONG DISCOURSES), ETC -- THERE ARE 5 NIKAYAS THAT CONSTITUTE A SCHEME FOR GROUPING THE PALI SUTTAS. I CONFESS THAT I HAVE NOT BEEN FATHFUL TO MY METHODOLOGY HERE AND HAVE NOT GIVEN A MORE ACCURATE TRANSLATION OF THE PALI TITLE. I AM CHANGING IT IN THE ENGLISH SECTION OF THE WEBSITE TO "A COLLECTION OF MIDDLE-LENGTH (DISCOURSES)" PLEASE DO THE SAME IN RUSSIAN, USING DISCOURSE AND NOT INSTRUCTIONS
Question: In Russian we have many meanings for the word “discourse”. Does it mean treatise here?
ALEX: YES, BUT A SPOKEN ONE
Question: I think we don’t have a word for “discourse” in this sense. We have this English word in Russian, but it has many meanings and it is quite scientific. Can we say “The Middle-Length Teachings”?
ALEX: OK

fields.Explanation:
ALEX: The text is an explanation of the main points of the Mahayana sutras and is one of the first Indian commentaries on Mahayana. So it is a beautiful elaborate piece of jewelry which is presented by its author as something to put on the sutras to adorn them and make them easier to understand. Thus it is a Filigree for the Mahayana Sutras, like a gift that the author is giving to the sutras
Question: Could we say "Ornament for the Mahayana Sutras". In Russian "filigree" is quite rare word. For instance, i didn't know the meaning of the word "filigree" until i faced it in someone's translation of your articles.
ALEX: IN ENGLISH, ORNAMENT SOUNDS PRETTY STRANGE, ALTHOUGH EVERYONE USES IT FOR RGYAN IN TITLES. RGYAN MEANS IS A VERY COMPLEX INTERTWINED ELABORATE PIECE OF JEWELRY. IF FILIGREE IS A WORD THAT NO ONE WOULD KNOW IN RUSSIAN, AND IF ORNAMENT DOESN;T SOUND LIKE A PIECE OF SCULPTURE DECORATING THE TOP OF THE OUTSIDE WALL OF A GREEK TEMPLE, THEN OK.

fields.Author:
Shantideva
Translit.: Zhi-ba lha
fields.Tibetan:
Full: bSlabs-pa kun-las btus-pa
Short: bSlabs-btus
fields.Explanation:
Question: For Compendium of Trainings we have several variants. In our current dictionary it is tranlated as "Compendium of Teaching", and in some article it is tranlated as "Compendium of all Disciplines". Should we translate it literally as "Compendium of Trainings"?
YES. USE TRAININGS. THIS IS A SPECIFIC TERM BSLAB-PA, AS IN THE THREE HIGHER TRAININGS. TEACHINGS IS BSTAN-PA. FOR EVERY DIFFERENT TIBETAN TERM, YOU NEED AS MUCH AS POSSIBLE A SPECIFIC DIFFERENT RUSSIAN TERM, LIKE I TRY TO DO WITH THE ENGLISH. TRY YOUR BEST NOT TO MIX TERMS. PLEASE READ THIS ARTICLE. IT IS ALREADY IN RUSSIAN ON THE WEBSITE: http://www.berzinarchives.com/web/en/archives/approaching_buddhism/modern_adaptation/recommendations/buddhism_west/guidelines_from_mongolian_experienc.html

fields.Term (raw):
Engaging in Bodhisattva Behavior
Popular: Bodhicharyavatara
fields.Author:
Shantideva
Translit.: Zhi-ba lha
fields.Tibetan:
Full: Byang-chub sems-dpa'i spyod-pa-la 'jug-pa
Short: sPyod-'jug
fields.Explanation:
Question: This Shantideva's text was published as "Entering into the Bodhisattva's Way". Does the word "engaging" have a meaning "entering" or does it have some other meaning? Which variant should we use?
ALEX: ENGAGING AND ENTERING ARE THE SAME WORD IN TIBETAN = 'JUG-PA. IT IS THE TERM USED IN ENGAGED BODHICHITTA, AS OPPOSED TO ASPIRING BODHICHITTA. IT MEANS TO ENETR INTO THE PRACTICE, WHICH MEANS TO ENGAGE IN THE PRACTICE, TO ACTUALLY DO IT. TRANSLATE MY TEXT TITLE EXACTLY AS IT IS : ENGAGING IN BODHISATTVA BEHAVIOR (NOT BODHISATTVA WAY). IF THERE IS A MORE FAMILIAR RUSSIAN TRANSLATION OF THE TITLE, PUT THAT IN PARENTHESES AFTER MY VERSION
Question: Can we translate it as "Practicing the Bodhisattva Behavior" or will it be not the same?
ALEX: NOT "PRACTICING" 'JUG-PA (SKT. AVATARA) MEANS TO ENTER INTO SOMETHING, TO ENGAGE IN DOING SOMETHING.
Question: We have the problem here, because in Russian it is impossible to say “engaging behavior”. That’s the reason why it was translated as “Engaging in Bodhisattva Way”. It is possible to say “Engaging in practice of Bodhisattva Behavior”.
ALEX: CAN YOU SAY ENGAGING IN BODHISATTVA CONDUCT, OR ENGAGING IN THE CONDUCT OF A BODHISATTVA. THAT WOULD BE BETTER.
Question: Unfortunately, there is one Russian word both for “behavior” and for “conduct”. So, there is the same problem.
ALEX: HOW ABOUT ENGAGING IN THE ACTIONS OF A BODHISATTVA.
Question: We also don’t say “engaging in the actions”. Can’t we say “Engaging the Bodhisattva Path” or “Engaging in the Practice of Bodhisattva Behavior”?
ALEX: ENGAGING IN THE PRACTICE OF BODHISATTVA BEHAVIOR IS OK. WE NEED THE WORD "BEHAVIOR" IN THE TITLE, SINCE IT IS THERE IN TIBETAN (SPYOD) AND SANSKRIT (CHARYA)
Gender of "Bodhicharyavatara": neuter

fields.Explanation:
Question: Our Russian word for “array” also means “construction”, so it would be possible to think that this sutra says how to build up the Pure Land of Bliss. Could we use the Russian word that means “arrangement”, “constitution”?
ALEX: THE WORD FOR ARRANGEMENT WOULD BE BEST
Question: This Russian word has many meanings, including “arrangement”, “constitution” and also “device”.
When we translate “The Sutra on the Array of the Pure Land of Bliss”, it is easy to understand that we mean “arrangement”,
ALES: SO USE THAT RUSSIAN WORD HERE.
Question: but when we translate “The Sutra on the Array Like a Woven Basket” using this word, it seems like “The Sutra on the device <that is> like woven basket”.
ALEX: DON'T USE THAT WORD HERE.
Question: Is it possible to use the word that means “structure” – “The Sutra on the Structure <that is> Like a Woven Basket”.
ALEX: NOT SO GOOD
Question: We have one more word for “arrangement”, which means arrangement/disposition/layout/order, and it seems to be quite suitable for “The Sutra on the Array Like a Woven Basket” (“The Sutra on the Disposition Like a Woven Basket”),
ALEX: USE THAT WORD HERE
Question: but if we use this word for “The Sutra on the Array of the Pure Land of Bliss”, it will be more like “The Sutra on the Location of the Pure Land of Bliss” – the meaning will be totally different.
ALEX: DON;T USE THAT WORD HERE.
SO, YOU WILL BE USING TWO DIFFERENT WORDS FOR ARRAY. THAT'S OK.

fields.Author: Dharmarakshita
fields.Explanation:
Question: Does it mean "The Whell with Sharp Weapons"?
ALEX: NO, IT LOOKS LIKE A THROWING STAR WEAPON THAT SAMURAI OR NINJAS USE. LIKE A WAGON WHEEL, WITHOUT THE OUSIDE RIM, AND THE SPOKES ARE MADE OF KNIVES.
Question: Is “The Wheel of Sharp Weapons” some kind of samurai weapon or does it only look like weapon? If the first, does it have some traditional name, which can be found in Wikipedia? If the latter, then what is it?
ALEX: IT IS THE WEAPON. THE JAPANESE NAME FOR IT IS SHURIKEN, BUT PLEASE DON'T TRANSLATE IT THAT WAY, SINCE NO ONE WILL KNOW WHAT IT IS, http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shuriken THE WHEEL OF SHARP WEAPONS WAS JUST THE TITLE THAT I MADE UP WHEN I FIRST TRANSLATED THE TEXT IN THE 1970'S. LITERALLY, THE WORD IN THE TITLE MEANS "WEAPON-WHEEL" OR "WEAPON-CIRCLE." IN MY NEW TRANSLATION, I MADE THE TRANSLATION OF THE WORD MORE PRECISE, AS THROWING STAR WEAPON. WHAT DO YOU SUGGEST IN RUSSIAN?
Question: Why has Dharmarakshita called hit text “The Wheel of Sharp Weapons”? What is the meaning of the name of the text in terms of it’s content?
ALEX: THE THROWING STAR WEAPON IS LIKE AN AUSTRALIAN BOOMERANG. YOU THROW IT OUT AND IT COMES BACK TO YOU. LIKE SUCH A WEAPON, THE NEGATIVE KARMA THAT WE CREATE, FROM DESTRUCTIVE BEHAVIOR THAT WE THROW OUT TO OTHERS, CIRCLES BACK TO US AND CAUSES SUFFERING TO US
Question: Is it possible to call shuriken "the weapon with sharp blades"?
ALEX: HOW ABOUT WHEEL WEAPON WITH SHARP BLADES. THE LITERAL TRANSLATION IS WHEEL OF SHARP WEAPONS.
Question: Concerning “Wheel Weapon With Sharp Blades”, does the word “Wheel” mean “round”, “circular” here?
ALEX: YES. IT LOOKS LIKE A STAR
“The Round Weapon with Sharp Blades” is not very good variant, because Russian word for “round” can also mean “spherical”. We can’t say “The Wheel Weapon”, because we need to say “The weapon in the form of a wheel”. We can’t say “The Wheel of Sharp Weapons”, because we can’t use genitive in this situation (it is impossible to say “the wheel of what? – the wheel of weapons”). We have two variants. One is “The Disc with Sharp Blades” – without “weapon”. The other is “The Weapon with Sharp Blades” – without “round”.
ALEX: DISC WITH SHARP BLADES.
